units.label: slide 4
units.text:
A real cipher that was actually cracked

The Zodiac Z408 Cipher — 1969
408 encrypted symbols 
used a homophonic substitution cipher 
one plaintext letter could have several different symbols 
solved by Donald and Bettye Harden 
they used guessed words — cribs 
one important guess was KILL / KILLING 
the repeated LL pattern helped reveal part of the key

units.label: slide 5
units.text:
Enigma – Predictable Messages

Enigma changed the substitution constantly using rotors. 
This created a huge number of possible settings. 
But many military messages had predictable content. 
Codebreakers could guess parts of the plaintext: 
weather reports 
standard phrases 
greetings and sign-offs 
repeated military wording 
These guesses helped eliminate many impossible Enigma settings.

units.label: slide 11
units.text:
Mars Robot Challenge
Robot commands:
Forward — 50% 
Right — 25% 
Left — 15% 
U-turn — 10%

We have 4 commands. If every code has the same length, how many bits do we need?

But, should FORWARD really use the same number of bits as U-TURN?
Design the shortest possible binary code you can for these commands.
every command needs a code, 
messages must be uniquely decodable, 
common commands should ideally have shorter codes.
